Symptoms.Diarrhoea: Watery, very frequent (about every waking hour), lasting 3 days, no blood seen, large volume.
Symptoms.Abdominal pain: Crampy, intermittent, mid-lower abdomen, moderate severity (6-7/10).
Symptoms.Nausea and vomiting: Nausea present, occasional vomiting especially after milk intake.
Symptoms.Fever: Subjective feeling of being hot, no measured temperature yet.
Symptoms.Other: No weight loss or other systemic symptoms mentioned.

step1_summary.Past medical history: No significant past medical history, generally fit and well.
step1_summary.Medications/allergies: No regular medications; occasional paracetamol for symptoms. No known drug allergies.

Family/social history.Social: Lives with mother and sister; brother also recently had similar diarrhoeal illness. Works in office, social smoking and occasional alcohol intake.

step1_summary.Vital signs/exam: No vitals or physical examination findings documented (teleconsultation).

V: Mesenteric ischemia: unlikely in young, no acute severe pain or risk factors but could cause diarrhoea and pain.
Viral gastroenteritis with possible dehydration-related hypotension.
I: Infectious gastroenteritis (viral, bacterial, protozoal): leading consideration based on acute watery diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, subjective fever, brother also affected.
Inflammatory bowel disease flare: less likely given no blood, no prior history.
N: Colon cancer: family history present; however, acute symptoms and patient age make this unlikely cause of acute diarrhoea.
D: Lactose intolerance or secondary to infectious enteritis: patient vomits after milk ingestion.
I2: Medication-induced diarrhoea: no regular medications to suggest this.
Toxin ingestion (food poisoning): possible, due to acute onset and family member affected.
C: Congenital malabsorption syndromes: unlikely given adult age and acute presentation.
A: Allergic gastroenteritis or food allergy: milk ingestion causing vomiting may point to intolerance or allergy but no rash or other systemic signs.
E: Endocrine diarrhoea (thyroid, diabetes): no symptoms to suggest this.
Electrolyte disturbances secondary to diarrhoea may cause symptoms.
